hints.content:
We are trying to find a **unit rate**, specifically the number of crabs seen per $1$ dive.

$\dfrac{\blueE{\text{crabs}}}{\maroonD{\text{dives}}} = \purpleD{\text{crabs per dive}}$

We can compare from the largest to the smallest place value.

###Finding the unit rates

We divide based on the unit rate we want.

Diver| $\blueE{\text{Crabs}}$ ||  $\maroonD{\text{Dives}}$||$\purpleE{\text{Crabs per dive}}$ 
- | :-: | :-:| :-:|:-:|:-:
Scuba Sam |$33$|$\div$ | $11$|$=$|$3$
Wet Suit Willy|$81$ |$\div$ |$18$ | $=$|$4.5$
Deep Diving Dan |$104$ |$\div$ | $26$|$=$| $4 $

###Comparing the unit rates

Diver | Ones | $.$ | Tenths
- | :-: | :-:| :-:|:-:|:-:
Scuba Sam | $3$ | $.$ | $0$
Wet Suit Willy| $\redE{4}$ | $.$ | $\redE{5}$
Deep Diving Dan | $\redE{4}$ | $.$ | $0$

Wet Suit Willy and Deep Diving Dan both saw $4$ ones of crabs per dive, but between those two, Wet Suit Willy saw the most tenths of crabs per dive.

###Conclusion

Wet Suit Willy saw the most crabs per dive.

question.content:
Three divers kept track of the number of crabs they've seen this year. 

Diver | Crabs observed | Dives
- | :-: | :-:
Scuba Sam | $33$ | $11$
Wet Suit Willy | $81$  | $18$
Deep Diving Dan | $104$ | $26$

**Which diver saw the most crabs per dive?**
